# Carpenter with a big mouth

Spot-breasted Woodpecker. Colaptes punctigula striatigularis​​​.

- [Start](https://www.eafit.edu.co/)
- [University Park](https://www.eafit.edu.co/universidad-parque)
- [Biotic Inventory](https://www.eafit.edu.co/universidad-parque/inventario-biotico)
- Buchipecoso Carpenter

[![Image of a woodpecker](https://universidadeafit.widen.net/content/73f6ea86-759e-4653-b9cc-6dc3089e6768/web/carpintero-buchipecoso.jpg)](https://www.eafit.edu.co/universidad-parque/inventario-biotico/carpintero-buchipecoso)

![](https://www.eafit.edu.co/universidad-parque/inventario-biotico/carpintero-buchipecoso)

###### Etymology

Colaptes, from the Greek kolaptes, to carve, to chisel. Punctigula, from the Latin punctum, to stain.

**Drawings: Daniela Peláez Vélez and Alejandro Arbeláez**

###### Description

It measures approximately 20 cm. It has a black forehead, a red crown extending to the nape; the back is yellow barred with black, the sides of the head are white, bordered below by a red mustache; the throat is mottled with black and white, the breast is yellow mottled with black, and the wings are yellow with black stripes. In females, the mustache is black and only the nape is red.

###### Ecology

It is found in open areas, edges, cultivated areas with scattered trees, várzea forests, and mangroves. It can be found alone or in pairs; occasionally, it is seen foraging on the ground. It nests in tree cavities that it digs itself. Breeding occurs between May and August. It feeds on insects, mainly ants.

###### Distribution

It can be seen up to 1500 meters above sea level. It has been reported throughout Colombia, except for the Pacific Coast, Guainía, and Vaupés. In the Aburrá Valley, it is commonly seen, as well as on the EAFIT campus, climbing tree trunks in search of food.
